A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CheXGenBench and contain readable main text, tables, figures, equations and appendices. Matching experiments and relocated material support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 11 generative models on MIMIC-CXR, including fidelity, privacy, classification, report generation and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds a LoRA-rank ablation for three large generative models in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The benchmark pipeline, model adaptation approach, metric computations and dataset-filtering stages remain unchanged. Higher-rank experiments are ablations, while expanded HealthGPT instructions document the existing filtering step without introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MIMIC-CXR generation, the same 14 condition categories, classification and report generation. Suggested out-of-distribution uses, segmentation and localization are applications or future directions, not additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The same 11 generative models and real-data downstream baselines participate in the retained comparisons. Appendix H varies LoRA configurations of existing models rather than introducing new comparator methods.

E3.justification: Appendix H adds LoRA ranks 64 and 128 alongside rank 32 for SD V3.5, Lumina 2.0 and Flux.1-Dev. Appendix F also revises the reported HealthGPT filtering prompt with explicit quality criteria; this does not establish that the dataset was regenerated. Main splits, budgets and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new LoRA-rank ablation tests whether greater adaptation capacity improves large-model fidelity. Existing caption, encoder, fidelity–utility, pathology-frequency and extended-Sana-training analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The privacy experiment still uses 10 random seeds for each of 2,000 prompts, and Table 6b retains the same plus/minus reporting. v3 introduces no new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 14 adds results under higher LoRA ranks, including rank-128 FID values of 74.58 for SD V3.5, 88.28 for Lumina 2.0 and 95.17 for Flux.1-Dev. Main benchmark results and earlier appendix results remain unchanged apart from reduced displayed precision in Table 3.

T1.justification: Appendix I reproduces the privacy-summary formulas previously in v1 Section 2.3. Their mathematical definitions are unchanged, and no new assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The central benchmark, model-performance and SynthCheX-75K claims persist. The introduction and conclusion additionally position CheXGenBench as an evidence source for synthetic-medical-data scorecards and a screening tool for subsequent radiologist MRMC studies.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges MIMIC-only evaluation and the absence of direct human evaluation. Appendix G adds single-institution demographic-bias and usage cautions, while Appendix H interprets the rank results as supporting thorough adaptation of smaller models.

D1.justification: Appendix G newly documents dataset licensing, storage size, labels, metadata and loading requirements. Appendix F supplies more detailed filtering instructions. Learning rates and hardware were already disclosed in v1; the newly numbered hyperparameter tables do not represent newly disclosed settings.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to TTT-Bench, SynFAC-Edit and Scorecards for Synthetic Medical Data Evaluation and Reporting, while retaining earlier cited works. The scorecard reference supports explicit complementary positioning and the new dataset card.

P1.justification: v3 condenses selected design and caption-description passages, expands the conclusion and adds appendix sections. Privacy-summary mathematics moves from Section 2.3 to Appendix I, but the main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 14 and boxed prompt/data-card displays, captions the existing hyperparameter tables as Tables 11–12, and relocates some main-text tables. Figures 1–4 are retained, and the earlier Sana report-generation table is renumbered from 11 to 13.

improvement.justification: The LoRA-rank analysis addresses a relevant sensitivity in the model comparisons, while clearer filtering documentation, the dataset card and explicit validation limits improve usability and interpretation. These are limited gains over the retained benchmark. A new reporting error partly offsets them: Table 14 gives a rank-128 average of 85.68, although its three entries average 86.01.
